correctness.rationale: The exact CoCD per-coordinate update matches the originating source. For a symmetric positive-definite two-coordinate quadratic, each central difference equals its partial derivative for every nonzero perturbation. The two-update sweep reduces exactly to the displayed 3x3 matrix; its characteristic cubic satisfies the four necessary-and-sufficient strict real Schur inequalities. Symbolic factorization reduces their joint feasible set to the smaller root of Q and proves the determinant threshold falls strictly between Q roots. Gamma-zero, rho-zero, and gamma-one endpoints are handled separately. At equality a unit-circle root prevents universal convergence, and above it spectral radius exceeds one; nonconvergence also affects actual iterates with zero buffer initialization. The entire parameter domain is proved analytically. The bundled script independently recomputes symbolic identities and adds non-exhaustive finite spectral checks.

value.rationale: The 2026 faded-coordinate algorithm motivates determining a usable fixed learning-rate boundary rather than relying on a restrictive sufficient bound. The new exact classification reveals the structurally counterintuitive effect that stronger coupling increases the stable step ceiling for strictly interior buffer retention and gives a sharp natural \(\alpha>2\) threshold with explicit stable parameters. This differentiates actual stability from the ordinary cyclic-coordinate step limit and can guide interpretation of stale-gradient memory; no broader optimization guarantee is claimed.
